title: Access Control and Identity Governance Policy
scope: This policy applies to workforce identities, service identities, privileged accounts, applications, infrastructure, and information assets managed or accessed by the organization.
principles: Access is granted from a documented business need and the minimum privileges required to perform an approved responsibility.
Identity ownership, authentication strength, and authorization decisions are accountable, traceable, and reviewed over time.
Privileged access is separately governed with stronger authentication, session accountability, and time-bounded elevation where practical.
Access is removed or adjusted promptly when employment, role, contract, asset, or business need changes.

requirements.statement: Every human and service identity must have a unique owner, a documented purpose, and an authoritative source record.
Access requests must be approved by the asset owner or delegated authority before access is provisioned.
Multi-factor authentication must protect remote, privileged, administrative, and high-impact application access unless a documented exception is approved.
Privileged access must use dedicated administrative identities, be logged, and be reviewed at least quarterly.
Access must be recertified on a risk-based cadence and removed within the defined service-level target after a triggering event.
Authentication and authorization failures must be monitored, protected from unauthorized modification, and investigated according to incident procedures.

exceptions.compensating_control: Document a compensating review, restrict the account to an approved network path, and record enhanced monitoring.
Use a time-boxed emergency identity, capture session evidence, and complete a post-event review.
